title: Win a Copy of the WHQ Chaos Adversary Cards
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7utAmGPE_M

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a giveaway for a brand new, unused copy of the Warhammer Quest Chaos Adversary Cards — an expansion long out of print and getting expensive — donated to the channel by online friend Sean Hanska.

The pitch for the cards is enthusiastic. They add a wide range of enemies to Silver Tower and Shadows Over Hammerhal, and Daniel reckons they elevate both games to a much higher status; he used them constantly during pre-COVID sessions of Shadows Over Hammerhal.

The memorable part is the condition attached. Sean and Daniel agreed the cards should be opened and played with rather than flipped, and Daniel says so on camera: he cannot enforce it, but he would be genuinely disappointed in a winner who put them straight onto eBay. It is an unusually explicit statement of the ethic behind the channel's giveaways — that scarce out-of-print material ought to end up on a table, not in a listing.

Entry is simple: like the video and comment that you want it. The contest closes when the channel crosses 3,000 subscribers, up from roughly 2,500 at the time of recording. Daniel expects to cover worldwide shipping, with a wry caveat about what might become of the American postal service in a few months.

----

Daniel asks the winner not to resell a scarce out-of-print expansion. Should giveaways come with strings like that, or is a gift a gift once it leaves your hands?
